notes: Known-answer navigation tasks for the javascript lane. Needle-based, not line-based: bench/verify-tasks/verify.mjs resolves every needle to a unique line at the current SHA, so the manifest survives edits without stale line numbers. Paths are relative to the lane root (javascript/), not to the repository root. 'expect' blocks carry the ground truth a harness scores against. A count is a minimum only where its field name starts with min_ (min_symbols, min_incoming); every other count is exact. On an implementation or cardinality task, exact_count counts concrete, non-generic, unconditionally computed impls only. On an implementation or cardinality list, optional_sites names declarations that satisfy the contract but are not counted (abstract base classes that extend it); a tool may return them or not. cfg-gated impls are excluded. On the implementation surface exact_count counts concrete classes only: JavaScript has no implements keyword, so satisfaction is structural and reached through the prototype chain, and the abstract bases (AbstractReport, AbstractPeriodicReport, AbstractCompositeReport, AbstractNotifier) are excluded from every count. Counting rules for the other count-bearing fields, each stated the way the current counts were made. references: a site is one line, so a line that names the symbol twice is one site. The lines searched are the .js, .cjs and .mjs files under packages/*/src and packages/*/tests; README prose, bench/ and the deliberately unparseable fixtures/broken-syntax files are outside the count. A line counts when the symbol appears on it as code (a call, member read, construction, argument, operand or assignment target), as a binding (an import or export specifier, a destructuring of require(...), a module.exports shorthand entry) or as a JSDoc type reference (an @param, @returns, @type, @property or @typedef type, including import("...").X and a local @typedef alias of the same name). It does not count when the symbol appears only in comment prose, only inside a string literal, or only as a property key of a JSDoc type literal ({ X: ... }), and the task's from line, which holds the declaration, is never counted. Each counted symbol has exactly one declaration in the lane, and every method call was checked to have a receiver of the declaring class, so every counted line refers to that declaration. exact_count on a references task is the number of counted lines: the known_sites entries plus the lines of every repeated_sites entry. repeated_sites names a needle written identically on several lines of one file; lines is the number of lines it matches, and each of those lines is one site. optional_sites on a references task names lines a tool may return or omit, outside exact_count: a JSDoc type-literal key, and for name_only the lines that carry the constant holding the string instead of the string itself. On a name_only task the counted lines are the code lines that write the literal string, the from line excluded. card-rule-contract: nominal_count counts the implementors declared as classes (one class per file under rules/, reaching the contract's members through its prototype), structural_count counts the plain object literals in rules/structural.cjs that carry the contract's members, and exact_count is their sum. multi-parent: extends_count counts the class's extends parent (one), implements_count counts the mixin objects Object.assign copies onto its prototype, and exact_count, where given, is their sum. call_hierarchy: min_incoming is a floor on the number of distinct callers, a caller being the innermost function, method or test callback that encloses a call line (the call lines themselves are not the unit); incoming_includes names one call line per caller. resolution: exact_count counts the declarations the call can dispatch to at run time, all listed under known_sites, and candidate is the one the default binding reaches. definition: known_sites names lines the answer passes through or rests on (a re-export hop, the import that brings in a built-in parent, a createRequire binding, a @template tag); they are context, not the answer, and carry no count unless the task states exact_count, in which case known_sites lists exactly the counted answers. must_not_include lists what a correct answer never contains: a namesake declaration of from.symbol or the file that holds it, the wrong end or direction of a parent edge, a re-export or barrel file the answer must pass through rather than stop on, a sibling name the import does not bind, and on a lane_local task a sibling lane's directory prefix. Kinds added by the fifth wave: builtin_parent (extends a node built-in), same_name (two exports with one name in different modules), jsdoc_generic (a JSDoc @template type parameter, which exists only in the comment and has no runtime form), dynamic_import (import() with a static specifier). Kind added by the implementation surface: structural (the implementor never names the contract, which is a JSDoc @typedef with no runtime declaration), glob (`export *`, whose exact_count is the number of names crossing the re-export), namespace_import (`import * as`, where the answer is the one member actually read off the namespace object). IDs shared with the php, rust, typescript, python and go lanes ask the same question in each language. document_symbol tasks count every named symbol the anchored FILE declares at any nesting depth (classes, members, functions, constants); each task's note enumerates that count N and states min_symbols = floor(0.75 * N), the 25% margin absorbing listings that fold container nodes. call_hierarchy tasks name callees under outgoing_includes and callers under incoming_includes; both are file+needle pairs the verifier resolves. Other kinds this lane uses: barrel (packages/core/src/index.js declares no name of its own and only forwards exports, so an import from @atelier/core resolves through it to the declaring module and never stops on the index file), mixin_parents (a class whose parents are one extends edge plus mixins copied onto its prototype with Object.assign: only the extends parent is visible at the class line, yet every one of them counts as a parent, either as exact_count or as extends_count plus implements_count), name_only (the subscribe call writes the event name "repair.completed" as a bare literal and no symbol reference links it to the emit path; the dispatch side may pass the REPAIR_COMPLETED constant, but only the matching string value ties the two together), shadow_alias (a rename of one of two same-name export class Formatter declarations, written as an ESM import { Formatter as X }, a CommonJS destructuring rename { Formatter: X } = require(...), or a JSDoc type written against such an alias: it resolves to the class in the module the import names, never its namesake), syntax_error (a negative-case fixture with an unclosed function or class body or an unbalanced destructuring pattern: any parser has to fail on it rather than invent closing braces and resolve halfway), type_only (a JSDoc type reference such as @type {import("...").X}, which creates no runtime edge: the file never requires the module it names). Kinds shared with other lanes, worded identically in every lane that uses them. child_of: the anchored declaration is the child end of a parent edge, and the answer is a direct parent it extends, implements or embeds, one level up, never a further ancestor and never one of its own children. imports: an import that binds only the names it lists; the answer is each named declaration in the file that declares it, never a sibling declared beside it and never every name the target module exports. lane_local: a symbol every lane carries under the same name or as its lane equivalent (Money, Customer, Dataset, the reference prefix, the invoice calculator's calculate, the billing Formatter); resolution must land on this lane's own declaration and never cross into a sibling lane. parent_of: a parent edge scored for direction, with the anchor at either end; the parent is the type that is extended, implemented or embedded, the child is the type that does so, and an answer that reports the child as the parent is wrong. unresolvable_static: an import whose target module is built from a runtime value, so no single module is the static answer; the honest result is every candidate module, and exact_count counts them. uses_self: a type that refers to itself, such as a tree node holding children of its own type; the edge is a uses edge back to the declaring type, never extends, implements or embedding. from.symbol is the identifier a task asks about, exactly as written on the from line and with no qualifier: the alias where an alias is used, the member on a member access, null when the question has no single identifier. from.occurrence (1-based) says which one when it appears more than once on that line, and is then required. document_symbol, parse-negative and diagnostics tasks ask about a file and carry neither key.
